title: vehicle-sil timeline (vehicle_sil_launch run --timeline), format 1
description: What a scenario run or manual recorded run did over the virtual time of one run: its steps (empty for manual runs), the values it wrote and the values it saw. Written by vehicle_sil_launch, read by tools that draw or compare a run. Every time is in milliseconds of virtual time and may have a fraction. A variable is named "<participant>.<name>" everywhere. A reader ignores keys it does not know, and does not draw (but names) a series, a watch or a step whose source, encoding, mode, op, kind or status it does not know: this schema therefore lists the values written today in the descriptions and does not close them, and allows more keys everywhere. Every key this schema lists is in every file (all are required, except conditional keys such as top-level recorded_to_ms on manual runs, variables[].recorded, and provenance/expect_skipped fields); a key that does not apply has the value null. The manual is docs/simulation-run.md of vehicle-sil.

vehicle_sil.description: The version of vehicle-sil that wrote the file.

stage.description: What the file is of: "run", a run that took place.

file.description: The simulation configuration, as it was named on the command line.

variant.description: The variant of the configuration that ran; null for a configuration without variants.

params.description: The scenario's parameters with the values in effect, as in `check --json`.

value.description: Its value, as a scenario reads it.

from.description: Where the value comes from (the scenario, the configuration, a variant, a case, a request file, or the command line).

time_step_ms.description: The time step of the launcher's controller (timing.time_step_ms of run --json): how often the scenario's engine looked at the samples and sent writes.

scenario.description: The scenario and its result, as in `run --json`, and up to when the series go; null for a manual run (--record, --record-events or --record-can without --scenario).

file.description: The scenario file, as it was named on the command line.

name.description: The scenario's name; null without one.

case.description: The named case that ran; omitted or null when the scenario has no cases.

status.description: "passed", "failed", "incomplete" (the simulation ended for another reason) or "not_run" (the simulation did not start).

over_at_ms.description: The step of the controller at which the scenario was over; null if it was not (incomplete, not_run). Usually after recorded_to_ms; at or before it only where a write was refused at once.

recorded_to_ms.description: The right end of the series: no point is later. Failed: the at_ms of the failed step (extended up to at_ms + record_after_fail_ms when --record-after-fail-ms / "record_after_fail_ms" is set on a normal assertion or wait-timeout failure, or the actual early-stop time if cut short during the tail; or the failed dither write when all steps had already passed; the time of the stop, if stop_at_ms ended the run). Passed: the latest at_ms of its steps (or up to min(end_ms, now) when end_ms is set). Incomplete: the time of the last sample that was looked at; or, if a write was refused and then a participant's failure became the result of the run, the time of that write. null if the scenario did not begin (the series are empty). In a failed run a step that passed may have an at_ms after it (it was decided before the failure was seen): its points are not in the series.

end_ms.description: The scenario's top-level end_ms (virtual time in milliseconds); null when the scenario omits end_ms.

recorded_to_ms.description: Manual runs only (when scenario is null): the right end of the recorded timeline in virtual time (ms) — stop_at_ms when the run ended at stop_at_ms, the latest recorded sample, event, or CAN frame time otherwise, or null if nothing was recorded. Omitted when scenario is an object (use scenario.recorded_to_ms).

variables.description: The variables the scenario uses, in the order of their first use.

name.description: "<participant>.<name>": how every other part of the file names the variable.

participant.description: The participant that has the variable.

causality.description: "input", "output" or "parameter"; null if the participant's description is not known.

min.description: The least value it takes, if it says one.

max.description: The greatest value it takes, if it says one.

value.description: The value that stands for it in the series.

ecu_step_ms.description: The step of its ECU (not the step of the variable's values).

written.description: A step of the scenario writes it: it has a series with the source "written".

watched.description: A condition of the scenario reads it: it has a series with the source "sampled".

recorded.description: Present and true only when the variable was explicitly requested via --record (or "record" in a request file / serve intent); omitted otherwise. Recorded variables always have a series with the source "sampled".

steps.description: The steps, in the order of the file: the keys of `run --json`'s scenario.steps[], and lines, watch and failed.

index.description: From 1, in the order of the file.

file.description: The scenario or template file that defines this step (omitted when it is the root scenario file).

line.description: Its line in the scenario or template file.

name.description: The human-assigned name of this step (omitted when the step has no name).

text.description: What it does, in one line, for people.

status.description: "passed", "failed", "unfinished", "not_run" or "skipped". The points that a step whose status is "passed" wrote were applied by the ECU: a step that writes (set, ramp, wave, dither) passes only once the ECU has applied every write of it (a dither's writes after its first are no step's).

start_ms.description: Its time; null if the scenario was over before it.

at_ms.description: The time that decided it; null if it was not decided.

end_ms.description: From where the next step counts; null if that is not known.

code.description: failed, skipped: the code of its finding.

expect_skipped.description: A ramp or a wave whose expect is not checked in this configuration: why.

call_stack.description: Template call chain from the root scenario down to this step (omitted for direct steps).

line.description: Line of the template call in that file.

name.description: Optional name on the template call step; null when omitted.

params.description: Resolved parameter values passed at this call site.

lines.description: Where the lines this step put are in the top-level lines[] (positions from 0); empty for a step that writes nothing, for one whose time is after scenario.recorded_to_ms, and for one that sent none of its writes.

watch.description: The conditions the step looks at and when; null for a step without conditions.

mode.description: "at": the values at from_ms (to_ms is null). "always": at from_ms and at every sample until to_ms (hold_for_ms). "once": at from_ms or at some sample until to_ms (within_ms, wait_until; when it became true is the step's at_ms). "during": at every sample of a time from from_ms to to_ms, and no value from before (the expect beside a ramp or a wave; to_ms is the ECU step that applies the end value, which may be later than the step's end_ms).

from_ms.description: Where the watch begins: the step's time. null if the scenario did not get to the step.

to_ms.description: Where the watch ends; null for the mode "at", and if the scenario did not get to the step.

conditions.description: One per variable: all must be true.

compare.description: The comparisons of its value: all must be true.

value.description: What the value is compared with; null when variable names a right-hand variable.

variable.description: The right-hand variable (<participant>.<name>) when comparing two variables; omitted for constant comparisons.

tolerance.description: near: how far the value may be from value or variable; null for the other ops.

failed.description: A failed step: what failed, as numbers (message says the same for people); null for any other step.

at_ms.description: The time of the failure: the sample that broke a condition, the time a wait ran out, the time of the write.

code.description: The code of the finding (scenario-failed, scenario-timeout, scenario-write, scenario-out-of-time).

conditions.description: The conditions that were not met (all of them, as the message joins them).

value.description: The value the variable had; null if it had none (no sample, non-finite, or none in the time of a "during" watch).

sample_ms.description: The time of the sample with that value; null with value.

compared.description: Right-hand variables of failed comparisons on this condition (omitted when no variable comparison failed).

value.description: The value the right-hand variable had; null if it had none (no sample, non-finite, or none in the time of a "during" watch).

sample_ms.description: The time of the right-hand variable's sample; null with value.

writes.description: A step that failed of a write: every write of the request that failed, in the order sent (what the step sent together for one time, for all its participants; of a dither's write that is no step's: what the dithers wrote for that time). Empty if the step did not fail of a write. An ECU takes its part of a request one write after the other and stops at the write it rejects, so the writes before that one are applied: applied says so for each. A step that failed before it sent anything (a variable that cannot be written, a ramp or a wave without a value to start from): the one write it could not make, with point null.

variable.description: The variable that was to be written.

at_ms.description: The time the write was for.

value.description: The value; null if it was never worked out.

point.description: The index in points of the variable's written series of the point that is this write; null if nothing was sent, or if the point went at a limit (limits.dropped).

applied.description: Whether the ECU applied this write. true: applied (the value is in the ECU, although the step failed). false: not applied (refused, rejected, behind the write that was rejected, or not sent). null: not known (no result came, or the ECU's result does not say which writes of its command took effect). A write with false or null that has a point is at or after not_applied_from of its series.

write.description: The index in writes, from 0, of the write that is the reason: the one the ECU or its agent named when it refused, or the only write of the participant that refused. null if no write is known to be the reason (the participant refused several writes as a whole without naming one, or no result came), and if the step did not fail of a write (writes is empty).

series.description: The values over the time, in the order of variables[] (of one variable the written series first). Only variables the scenario uses have series.

source.description: "written": the values the scenario sent, each with the time it was for; sent, not necessarily applied (not_applied_from). "sampled": the values of the ECU's samples that the scenario looked at; a sample has the value at the end of an ECU step and the time of its start, so a value holds from its point to the next.

encoding.description: "all": every value is a point (written). "changes": a point only where the written text of the value differs from the one before (sampled).

samples.description: sampled: how many samples there were up to recorded_to_ms (also those whose points a limit dropped). null for written.

first_ms.description: sampled: the time of the first sample; null without a sample, and for written.

last_ms.description: sampled: the time of the last sample (the last point holds until there); null without a sample, and for written.

not_applied_from.description: written: the index in points from which on the points were sent and are not known to have been applied by the ECU. They are the first write of a failed request that was not applied or has no result (failed.writes[].applied of the failed step is false or null; its point is this index or after it) with what was sent after it, and the points for a time after scenario.over_at_ms (no ECU got to that time). Do not draw them as values the variable took. null if there are no such points, and for sampled. In a run that did not pass, a point before it may still not have been applied (the run ended before its result was looked at).

columns.description: What a point is: ["at_ms", "value"], and ["at_ms", "value", "base"] for an input that the scenario puts a dither on (its inputs, or a dither step with a shape that runs in this configuration; whether the run got to it does not matter). base is what the value was made of before the dither was added and the variable's type applied: the value of a set, the value of a ramp or a wave at that time. A reader takes the columns it knows by name.

points.description: What columns says ([at_ms, value] or [at_ms, value, base]), one per line of the file. at_ms never goes back; points of one time are in the order sent. A bool is true or false, an enum the value of its item, a real that is no number null.

lines.description: The lines of the inputs: what each step put on the line of a variable it writes when its time came (a set its value, a ramp or a wave its motion), in the order put: by time, then by step, then in the order within the step. A dither is a line too (kind "dither"): from the first write that carried it, after the lines that the steps put at that time; the next dither line of its variable is where it ends. Only those put at or before scenario.recorded_to_ms of which a write was sent (also one that was refused): a line whose first write the scenario did not get to, because a write before it failed, is not here. Empty for a run that never began.

kind.description: The kind of the step: "set", "ramp" or "wave"; "dither" for a dither (of a dither step, or one that the scenario's inputs declare). A reader skips a line of a kind it does not know.

file.description: The scenario or template file that defines this step or input entry (omitted when it is the root scenario file).

line.description: The step's line in the scenario or template file; of a dither that the inputs declare, the line of its entry.

step.description: The step's index (steps[].index); null for a dither that the inputs declare (it is no step's).

from_ms.description: The step's time: from here the line has this value or motion. Of a dither: the time of the first write that carried it (a dither waits for the first value a step puts on its input).

to_ms.description: The end of the motion as the text says it (from_ms and its length); of a set from_ms. A run that ended earlier wrote the points up to scenario.recorded_to_ms only. null for a dither: the text gives it no end, and it is there until the next dither line of its variable.

base.description: Of a set its value. Of a ramp or a wave what it starts from or swings around, written as a point of a series is (a number the step names is written as it is); null if the shape has its values itself.

base_source.description: Where base is from: "written" (the step names it: a set's value, from, around, the other value of a bool), "line" (where the scenario left the variable: the value of its line at from_ms), "sample" (the scenario had not written the variable: its latest sample then, which may depend on time_step_ms); null without a base.

shape.description: Of a ramp, a wave or a dither: the shape with the values the text gives, the parameters put in (what the text leaves out is not here, nor from and around: see base). It is for showing the line; the values are in the series. null for a set, and for a dither step's none (the dither is taken off).

type.description: "ramp", or the wave's shape ("sine", "triangle", "sawtooth", "square", "pulse", "noise", "chirp", "lag", "chatter", "points"). The other keys are those of the shape in the scenario (a ramp: to, over_ms; a wave: its keys and for_ms). Of points: points (how many), interpolate, and of points from a file its file, value, time and time_unit as given (the values are in the series).

text.description: The line as the step's text has it, for people.

events.description: Opt-in virtual-timestamped structured ECU control events (control::Agent::log / Ecu::log) recorded up to recorded_to_ms when --record-events (or "record_events": true) is set; omitted otherwise. Ordered by virtual time at_ms (then participant and emission order). Raw child stdout/stderr pipes carry wall-clock times only and are not included.

at_ms.description: The ECU simulation step time in virtual milliseconds at which the event was logged.

participant.description: The participant whose control agent emitted the event.

text.description: The event message text (truncated at control::wire::kMaxTextBytes on the wire if longer).

can_frames.description: Opt-in virtual-timestamped CAN frames observed by passive SIL Kit CAN observers up to recorded_to_ms when --record-can (or "record_can": true) is set; omitted otherwise. Ordered by virtual time at_ms (then network and arrival order). Grounded virtual timestamps apply to time-synchronized virtual-time participants (sender step time or CanBusSimulator arbitration end time); frames arriving with SIL Kit event.timestamp < 0 (such as from unsynchronized senders before SimulationController's first step) are dropped and counted in limits.can_dropped[].untimed_dropped rather than stamped with a fabricated timestamp. Once virtual time is running (t >= 0), SIL Kit's synchronized receiver stamps frames from unsynchronized/real-time senders (e.g. external bridges in mixed runs) with the controller's current virtual step time before the frame handler runs.

at_ms.description: Virtual timestamp of the CAN frame in milliseconds (SIL Kit CanFrameEvent::timestamp: sender step time or CanBusSimulator arbitration end time for time-synchronized participants, or the controller's current virtual step time stamped by SIL Kit for unsynchronized senders once t >= 0).

network.description: The CAN network name from the simulation configuration.

id.description: The CAN arbitration identifier (11-bit standard 0..2047 when extended is false; 29-bit extended 0..536870911 when extended is true).

extended.description: true for a 29-bit extended CAN ID (IDE); false for an 11-bit standard CAN ID.

data.description: The frame payload encoded as an uppercase hexadecimal byte string (empty string when zero payload bytes or RTR).

rtr.description: Present and true only for Remote Transmission Request (RTR) frames; omitted otherwise.

fd.description: Present and true only for CAN FD frames (FDF); omitted otherwise.

findings.description: The findings of the check and of the run that are about the scenario (code scenario-...), as in `run --json`; and control-link-late-values (an ECU's values came later than promised: what such a run recorded may differ from run to run) with its severity and code only, the rest null. No other finding: nothing of the run's pace in real time.

code.description: The fixed name of the finding.

message.description: What is wrong and what to do, for people; null for control-link-late-values.

limits.description: How many points the file keeps, and what went. Beyond a limit the oldest points of a series go and the newest stay. Counted are the points of samples and the written points of a ramp or a wave; the written points of a set always stay. A run that dropped points also says so in its result (the note timeline-limit).

points_per_series.description: The most points of one series.

points_total.description: The most points of all series together; beyond it the series with the most points give first.

dropped.description: The series that lost points; empty if none did.

dropped_from_ms.description: The time of the oldest point that went. From here up to (not with) dropped_before_ms values are missing: do not join points across this time. In a written series the points of a set stay, also in and before this time; the values of the ramp or wave between them and dropped_before_ms are not there.

dropped_before_ms.description: The time of the oldest point that stayed, of the points that can go (all of a sampled series; of a written series those of a ramp or a wave).

events_per_participant.description: Present when --record-events is enabled: the most ECU events kept per participant; omitted otherwise.

events_total.description: Present when --record-events is enabled: the most ECU events kept across all participants together; omitted otherwise.

events_dropped.description: Present when --record-events is enabled: participants that lost ECU events at the timeline limits or inside their Agent queue; empty if none did; omitted otherwise.

participant.description: The participant whose events were dropped.

dropped.description: How many older events were evicted by the timeline limits.

dropped_from_ms.description: The virtual time of the oldest event evicted by the timeline limits; null if dropped is 0.

dropped_before_ms.description: The virtual time of the oldest event that stayed for this participant; null if dropped is 0 or none stayed.

agent_dropped.description: How many events the participant's control Agent dropped before they reached the Hub, when reported by the transport (SIL Kit wire v2 currently reports 0).

can_frames_per_network.description: Present when --record-can is enabled: the most CAN frames kept per network; omitted otherwise.

can_frames_total.description: Present when --record-can is enabled: the most CAN frames kept across all CAN networks together; omitted otherwise.

can_dropped.description: Present when --record-can is enabled: CAN networks that lost frames at the timeline limits or dropped untimed frames (event.timestamp < 0); empty if none did; omitted otherwise.

network.description: The CAN network whose frames were dropped.

dropped.description: How many older frames were evicted by the timeline limits.

dropped_from_ms.description: The virtual time of the oldest frame evicted by the timeline limits; null if dropped is 0.

dropped_before_ms.description: The virtual time of the oldest frame that stayed for this network; null if dropped is 0 or none stayed.

untimed_dropped.description: How many frames were rejected because SIL Kit delivered event.timestamp < 0 (for example from unsynchronized senders before SimulationController's first step) rather than fabricating a virtual timestamp.
